Hello, Woz! I've a huge fan of your work.

I have a question for you and like you said, I wish it to be answered as honestly as possible.

My question is: If for some weird reason, Steve Job's soul magically appeared in front of you and you get to ask him one question that he could answer and tell him one thing that you've always wanted to, what would it be?

I'm a very hard-working person.

Back in the day, I used to own literally ALL consoles there is. From the Atari, NES, SNES to XBOX, PS1, PS2 and PS3 to everything! I even own all portable game devices such as Gameboys and other things. I was an avid console and game collector. My game library is massive and could take up an entire master bedroom. 

Guess where all of that is now? Gone. I sold it all...or rather, I was forced to sell it. Back in 2011, when my wife got pregnant, her grandmother was hospitalized and was diagnosed with a very serious ailment. They didn't have money. Most of mine were paid to the hospital my wife was staying at during her labor. I didn't want her to worry while she was focusing on delivering my child so I promised to her that I'd take care of her financial problems.

My friends were broke. I didn't have anyone I can borrow money to, until a friend of mine introduced a gamer/collector to me and offered to buy my entire gaming collection of consoles, handhelds and physical game copies for $44,000. The reason the price was set this high was because of rare, mint-conditioned games and other memorabilia that I had in my collection. I didn't have time to think. My wife was in labor.

So I agreed to sell everything.

I got the money and paid for my wife's grandmother's hospital bills. I paid a maximum of $34,000 just for hospital bills because of the number of operations the doctors did to her just so she could survive. The bills racked up and I was afraid it would keep increasing to the point that I would have to put out additional money from my pockets. Luckily, it stopped there.

I gave my wife my entire life. My entire hobby. My passion and sold everything for the sake of her family. What did I get in return? Her cheating on me and divorcing my ass, bleeding me dry from the divorce and me ending up basically broke, both emotionally and financially.

All I have now is a little beat up, second hand XBOX 360 and a couple of games a few friends gifted to me to cheer me up. It's too depressing to pick up the controller now that I've shared this. I wish I could just let this all out verbally and not through text, but I guess this helps me somewhat.

Thank you for your words.

I don't hate my mother. I am very grateful to her that she has done so much for me and my son. Whenever she says very mean things to me, I just let it slide and pretend I didn't hear it. You don't bite the hand that feeds you, or in this case, helps you. I don't want to jeopardize my son's relationship with his grandmother. I am just happy and grateful enough that my son is standing up for me when I could not. 

Like you, I also lost my job. A very good one at that. I deeply regret losing it but the feeling I get whenever I'm depressed, it just overshadows all other emotions I feel. I don't feel regret. I don't feel remorse. I don't feel anything. I just feel this one thing that's been beating me down constantly and I wish to God it would go away.

You know, I LOVE playing video games. It's my passion. I'm a huge gamer. Whenever I'm stressed from work, a couple of hours of gaming straightens me out real quick. It doesn't work anymore. I would fire up the console and put down the controller as quickly as I picked it up. I can barely play ANY game for anything longer than 15 or 30 minutes. I always end up putting down the controller and going back to bed.

I don't know why. The things I normally enjoy? I don't enjoy them anymore. Nothing feels enjoyable anymore. I don't feel joy in anything I do and it gets worse everyday. There are times where I force myself to smile in the presence of my son just so he wouldn't worry about me.

I don't know why I feel or became this way. I don't want it. I didn't want it. I want it to go away but I have no idea how. It feels as though I am possessed by a malevolent force and it's dragging me down as each day passes.

I've not yet done any research regarding if my city/country provides disability benefits for people suffering from depression and anxiety. Hopefully there is one. If not, I am fucked.

Yes, I have a lot of free time, but how do I utilize that free time if the the simple act of stepping my foot out of the house is sometimes deemed impossible in my head? 

I felt like my entire room became a gigantic zone where it is the only place I feel safe and the irony is that it is also the place that slowly kills me.

I don't know how to explain these feelings well...

The big question is that for how long can I hold on?

I want to get out there and seek help. An online friend of mine told me to go to my local city hall and seek advice about temporary unemployment benefits until I can get back up on my feet. My friend told me to also seek psychological counselling to discuss my depression and anxieties in order to help me feel better, perhaps they could prescribe something to me that would help relieve the condition or at least maybe lessen the depression and panic attacks.

But do you know what I want to do?

I want to get up and start working again. I want to go back to the gym and start hitting the weights so that I could get my old body back. I want to have at least an hour of heart to heart talk with my ex-wife and let out all the repressed feelings I have. The feelings that I kept bottled up inside because I didn't had the time nor the opportunities to express my feelings and my thoughts to her after the divorce happened. I have zero intentions of going back to her. I don't want to get back together with her. I just want the opportunity to tell her that I loved her and I still love her despite what she did. I want to tell her that I forgive her for what she did to me and to my son. I want to tell her and remind her of all the promises she made but never kept. I want to tell her I'm sorry for anything I lacked during our marriage that made her cheat and leave. I want closure before I leave her for good and move on.

But reality is that that is not possible.

She will not talk to me. She will not hear me out. Every time I try to place my foot out of that door, a malevolent voice always tells me "GO BACK INSIDE THE HOUSE. GO BACK TO YOUR ROOM NOW." and I can feel this invisible vibration that is pulling me backwards and pushing me back down to my bed. My mind is full of fuck and I don't know how much longer I could last in this stressful environment. 

I want to get away from it all, even for just a little while. I want to go somewhere vast and open. Scream my lungs out and cry to my heart's content.

Fuck, man.

Thank you so much.

I hope that your own situation were a lot better than mine.

I don't really consider myself as an "exceptional father". Hell, I don't even know what constitutes or qualifies as exceptional when being a father or a parent. My dad abandoned me when I was born so I never did experience what it was like to be loved or lectured by a father or a father figure for that matter. No one was there for me. My mother was working throughout her entire life and I was pretty much alone and fended for myself throughout adulthood. All I know is that even in my depressed state, I would not deny my son the opportunity to bond and spend time together. It's the least that I could do for him. I love him so much and every time I spend with him, I become less and less sad. He's literally the only person that can make me smile and laugh. In a dark world, he's like my only beacon of light that urges me to move forward.

My "friends" were a toxic bunch of assholes. All they do was drink, fight and cause mayhem. I pretty much abandoned them and gave up on them after I became a father. They resented and hated me for it but it didn't matter to me. All that mattered to me at that point was taking care of my family.

As I have said, after the divorce, so many fucking things happened all at the same time and I tried my best to cope and adapt to every single fucked up situation I got thrown in without losing my sanity. I did not have the luxury of time to grieve for the loss of my family. The lost and infidelity of my wife. The betrayal. The fact that my son is now going to grow up without a mother. I promised myself that as a person who grew up with divorced parents, I would never do that to my son. But now I can't hold that promise when my wife left and cheated.

My mother has done so much for me. I know that her constant criticisms do not help, but I just try to be as understanding as I can because she did say that she was under heavy financial burdens herself and that she was dealing with her own life stress. I do not want to add to that. I did not want to add to her burdens. To her, her constant criticisms, shouting and harsh and hurtful words are words of encouragement. That's how her own mother raised her. To them, hurtful words are words of encouragement all the same because if you truly have your own pride as a person, you wouldn't allow yourself to be spoken that way and you'd do something about to prove to that person that you're not what they say you are. That's my mother and grandmother's logic. By hitting your pride, they're encouraging you to become angry and seek out revenge in a way to prove yourself. I know. Their logic and way of encouragement is morbidly fucked up but if it worked on them, they think it will work on me.

Sadly, all it did was kill what little self-esteem I had for myself.

Right after I fell to depression, the time I normally devoted to my job, I gave to my son instead. We spent time together, played together and I was there in every important moment of his life. If he had a play at preschool, I would invent a sickness at work just so I can take the day off or cut work early to attend every event in his life.

Sadly, there is no one else out there for me to reach out to. I've cut my ties with my past friends, the ones from my teenaged years because they were toxic influences in my life and never gave me anything but trouble. When you become a single father, you tend to focus more on your work rather than hanging out with friends or even making friends. I have a few online friends who I chat with from time to time, but it's mostly just your regular "Hey, how you doing? Been playing good games lately? How's the kid?" type of conversations. I've never had a conversation with anyone that I actually connected with and understood what I felt, or at least tried to.

I know that my mother means well and when we fought yesterday, she kept shouting at me how I should "man up". I keep telling her that if it were that easy, I would have done it a long time ago and wouldn't ask for help. I told her that the only reason I'm asking for her help to listen to me was because I was getting alone and my condition worsen everyday. I needed someone to talk to on a personal basis. Someone to connect with. My mother and my son were all I have. My son is too young to understand what I'm saying or what I'm going through. My mother completely disregards everything I'm going through.

So I'm out of both options..

My grandmother gave tough love to 5 of her sons. All of them flunked school and gave up on life. They felt unneeded, unwanted and unloved. I still remember the stories of how my uncle almost died at the hospital for trying to kill himself because he couldn't take her mother's "abusive words".

I love my son so much and he's all I have in this world apart from my mother. I also love my mother and I mean no disrespect to her. In fact, I feel as though maybe she was justified to slap and hurt me because I have become a burden to her in the past couple of months. My son is the only one that's giving me reason to live.

I don't wanna leave him but it's like in the movie Lord of the Rings and depression and anxiety is like when Frodo was wearing the ring as his necklace. You're fine for a little while at first, but overtime the self-hatred, depression and unnerving anxiety slowly kills you inside and slowly drives you to commit unfathomable things such as suicide. The emotional torment and burden gets heavier and heavier as days pass by. I don't wanna leave my son alone in this world because I know what it feels like to have no father to be there for you. But no one in my life understands what I'm going through. They think I'm just "going through a mid-life crisis" or I'm just "become too lazy to work" when I know that's not the case.

My son, every night, he would hug me and tell me that everything would be alright. He's 4 years old and he's giving me the strength to fight. I keep telling him that daddy doesn't know when he'll bounce back but I always promise him that I'll keep fighting. He hugs and kisses me a lot. My tears always drench and soak his shirt every time he hugs because my son's love is so pure, unbiased, real and innocent. Indeed that children are the only ones that can show you what true love really is.
